title.narrative: Sustaining Lifesaving Health Services in Deir-ez-Zor

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to the global humanitarian overview, in 2025, Syria remains a global humanitarian crisis, with 16.5 million people in need of assistance and 7.4 million internally displaced (IDP) persons. The conflict and its aftermath continue to create widespread displacement and hardship, with a significant portion of the population living in IDP camps or relying on humanitarian aid. The international community has pledged over $3.19 billion to address humanitarian and socio-economic needs in Syria and its neighboring countries in 2025, but the needs remain significant, with a substantial funding gap. These shortages have disrupted life-saving services including immunization, reproductive, child health, and mental health services disproportionately affect women and children. Health facilities (HFs) face shortages of trauma kits, ambulances, essential medicines, and blood supplies. (OCHA, 2025) Additionally, Syria’s economic decline has deepened vulnerabilities, especially for women and girls, who face rising early marriage, domestic violence, and economic dependence. This underscores that health care services need to be accessible, adequately resourced, and tailored to meet the specific needs of vulnerable populations while effective coordination with humanitarian and health partners is critical to address protection concerns. (OCHA_ Humanitarian Situation Report April 2025) ltbrgtltbrgtRelief International (RI) proposes a six-month health intervention in Deir-ez-Zor (DeZ), Northeast Syria (NES) serving an estimated 70,760 crisis affected individuals The proposed health project will deploy two mobile medical units (MMU) across seven underserved villages-Al Husainia, Hatla, Khasham, Tabiyet Jazira, Mathlum, Sadouni, and Mrat - to provide essential life-saving health care and referral support services to vulnerable, hard-to-reach populations, thereby reducing the pressure on existing facilities. Additionally, RI will support, Jezrat Comprehensive Primary Health Center (CPHC) and Mhemideh Basic Primary Health Center (BPHC) through incentives, prepositioning of medicines and commodities, referrals and provide technical and management support, provide operational support, running costs, maintenance, and training for healthcare workers, ensuring sustained service provision and improved maternal and neonatal health outcomes. ltbrgtltbrgtThe scope of the project will include provision of primary health care services including outpatient consultations, prevention and management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, treatment for injuries and first aid, mental health consultation, provision of Reproductive Health (RH) services such as Ante Natal Care (ANC), Post natal care (PNC), Family planning (FP) consultation and treatment of Sexually transmitted infections (STIs), nutrition screening and treatment for malnutrition, and health and nutrition promotion. In addition, Jazrat CPHC will provide assisted deliveries and Basic Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (BEmONC) services. This project will establish a strong referral structure between the MMUs and nearby health facilities as well as between PHCs and secondary health care facilities. RI will deliver essential medicines, medical supplies, equipment, and materials to all supported HFs. RI will provide support to the Department of Health (DOH) in epidemic disease surveillance and outbreak response. ltbrgtltbrgtThe project ensures inclusive access by tailoring health services to the specific needs of diverse population groups. Women and girls receive reproductive and maternal health care, while children benefit from curative and preventive health and nutrition services. Men and boys are included in outpatient care, trauma care, mental health and health education. MMUs reach remote communities, and strong referral systems link patients to higher-level care. The project also builds local health worker capacity in inclusive practices and supports epidemic surveillance to protect at-risk groups. ltbrgtlt/pgt
